text:
University College London (UCL) was founded on February 11, 1826, as London University, initially functioning as a joint stock company and lacking official university status. It later evolved into University College, London, by royal charter on November 28, 1836. In 1878, the University of London granted a supplemental charter allowing UCL to award degrees to women, which UCL admitted in 1878 for the Faculties of Arts, Law, and Science.
UCL surrendered its legal independence to the University of London in 1907, becoming a school of that university. It regained legal independence in 1976 and became formally known as University College London. In 2005, UCL gained its own taught and research degree-awarding powers. UCL is a founding member of the Russell Group and is part of the 'golden triangle' of research-intensive universities alongside Cambridge and Oxford. The university is organized into eleven faculties, each containing schools, departments, and institutes.
